Lessons.Title: Paper Clip Games (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Create and play a number-line fraction game.
Key idea: Fraction benchmarks mark positions along an evenly partitioned number line; game rules should make outcomes comparable and fair.
How to reason: Locate the interval 0 to 2, subdivide equal whole units and justify a mark between benchmark numbers.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Lots of Paper Clips (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unit intervals and comparison
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fraction's position is defined relative to one fixed unit interval.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Write all positions in fourths before comparing or scoring a paper-clip game.
KeyConcepts.Example: 3/2 is 6/4, so 7/4 lies to its right.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independently authored source-aligned model
WorkedExamples.Question: A clip lands at 5/4 on a 0-to-2 board. Is it to the right of 1?
WorkedExamples.Method: Locate the interval 0 to 2, subdivide equal whole units and justify a mark between benchmark numbers.
Steps: Every interval from 1 to 3/2 is one half wide.
The mark lies right of 1 and left of 3/2.
WorkedExamples.Check: Exact rational calculation confirmed; source example not copied.

WorkedExamples.Title: Edulytics independent model: a clip at seven fourths
WorkedExamples.Question: On an evenly divided 0-to-2 number line, is 7/4 to the left or right of 3/2?
Steps: Rewrite 3/2 as 6/4 without changing the whole.
Compare 7/4 with 6/4 on the same marked interval.
Since 7>6, the clip at 7/4 is 1/4 to the right of 3/2.
WorkedExamples.Check: New first-party numeric illustration; actual original paper-clip toss is teacher reviewed.

WorkedExamples.Title: Edulytics independent model: two scored clip landings
WorkedExamples.Question: A clip lands at 3/4 on one attempt and at 5/4 on the next. Which landing is greater?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the same fourth-unit benchmark and compare numerators.
Steps: Partition each whole into four equal intervals.
Locate 3/4 before 1 and 5/4 one fourth beyond 1.
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher reviews any physical-game rule or hand-drawn number line.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Placing a fraction by counting ticks without verifying the unit interval changes its value.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It does not preserve the intended mathematical relationship or original task condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Locate the interval 0 to 2, subdivide equal whole units and justify a mark between benchmark numbers.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Placing 7/4 to the left of 3/2 because 4 is less than 2.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Denominators label subdivisions, not the size of the number alone.
